title: Recovery Concurrency and Rollback Safety
recoveryGuarantees: Fenced transition: updateReleaseIntentStatusIfOwned only succeeds when the caller's workerId holds a live (non-expired) lease on the intent. Returns { updated: false } for a stale worker; the caller must stop.
Renewal fencing: renewReleaseIntentLease requires lease_expires_at > now. An expired worker cannot revive its lease; a superseded worker cannot renew.

Atomic SQL conditional: the fenced transition is a single UPDATE ... WHERE intent_key = ? AND leased_by = ? AND lease_expires_at > ? [AND status IN (...)]. Zero rows affected means the worker is fenced; the JS-side check is not authoritative.
First-mutation fencing: the AUTHORIZED -> DEPLOYMENT_INTENT_CREATED path now acquires the lease before transitioning, so even the initial recovery write is fenced identically to later writes.
Recovery executor fully fenced: all 19 intents.transition(...) call sites in release-recovery-executor.ts are transitionIfOwned(..., this.deps.workerId, ...).
Rollback path already fenced: markFailedAndRollback and resumeRollback acquire the lease before any mutation; all transitions inside them use transitionIfOwned.
UNKNOWN provider outcome remains RECOVERY_REQUIRED: an owner may write RECOVERY_REQUIRED with providerStatus=UNKNOWN; a stale worker cannot transition it to KNOWN_GOOD or clear the recovery reason.
Cross-project integrity: projectId cannot be overwritten by a patch and is preserved through every transition; two intents from different projects remain isolated in the store.
Crash matrix: after a worker crashes without releasing, the lease expires, a new worker acquires authoritatively, the crashed worker is fenced on all attempted mutations, and durable state persists.
Expected-status guard: transitions can be gated to an expected status set; mismatch -> not updated, status preserved.
Store enforces ownership, not state-machine validity. Terminal-state immutability (ALREADY_KNOWN_GOOD etc.) remains the classifier's concern, per the existing recovery model.
